title: Concise polyglot adapters for streaming + retries (Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP, CLI)
creator: Aisha Puri
description: Create a small, opinionated set of example adapters and cookbook snippets across Python, TypeScript, and Go that demonstrate idiomatic streaming ergonomics and robust retry patterns for Redwood's SDKs. Deliverables include: a Next.js edge example for streaming responses to the browser, a FastAPI server example showcasing server-side streaming + resumable retries, a minimal Go HTTP server with context-aware cancellation and per-request retry policies, and a CLI example that shows streaming progress and safe retry/backoff behavior. The goal is targeted: concise code paths developers can copy into apps with minimal plumbing and clear guidance on trade-offs (latency vs. batching, at-most-once vs. at-least-once semantics, idempotency keys).
acceptance_criteria: Next.js example: client-side streaming using Redwood streaming connector + TypeScript wrapper, <10 files, documented in README
FastAPI example: server streaming endpoint that supports resuming after transient failures using tokenized KV caching and idempotency key; tests that simulate network drop
Go HTTP server: example shows context cancellation propagation, 2 retry strategies (exponential backoff + jitter, and fixed small immediate retries), and a short README with recommended defaults
CLI example: shows progress bars for streaming tokens, safe ctrl-c handling, and deterministic retry for failed network calls
All examples include: minimal install steps, one-liner run commands, and links to corresponding GitHub PRs and CI checks
technical_notes: Python: expose streaming as an async iterator with a small helper that converts SDK deltas into text chunks; prefer explicit close()/aclose() to ensure KV cache flushes
TypeScript (Next.js): use ReadableStream for streaming to the edge, provide a small wrapper that optionally buffers first N tokens to avoid broken HTML when embedding in a page
Go: use context.Context deadlines for cancellation, attach request-level metadata (idempotency-key, client-version) to enable safe retries on server-side

Retries: default policy = exponential backoff with jitter + max attempts = 4; for idempotent calls recommend at-least-once with idempotency-key, for non-idempotent use circuit-breaker and fewer retries
Batching trade-offs: include a short note on how enabling batching reduces token cost but increases tail latency; examples include toggles to demonstrate the difference
Observability: instrument examples with basic timing and error logs; include a pointer to Console dashboard queries to reproduce per-route latency histograms
rollout_plan: Merge example PRs into sdk-examples repo behind a single umbrella PR. Add docs/snippets to docs.redwood.ai/examples with code sandbox links for Next.js and playground for Python. Announce in weekly SDK sync and add to onboarding checklist for Developer Experience.
risks: Edge runtime differences between Vercel and local Node may confuse users — mitigate with explicit 'tested on' matrix in README
Retry semantics may give illusion of reliability for non-idempotent operations — call out in READMEs and include an example of using idempotency keys
Streaming API changes could require example updates when runtime kernels change — keep examples small and rely on SDK helpers rather than internal runtime details
test_plan: Unit tests for adapter helpers (Python async iterator, TypeScript ReadableStream wrapper, Go retry helper)
Integration tests that run a local FastAPI server and a Go server and assert correct resume behavior after injected network errors
CI job that builds Next.js example and runs Lighthouse smoke test for streaming correctness
Manual review: SDK team walkthrough + DevRel quickstart verification

2025-11-10: Engineering review (Marco Chen) — decided on default retry policy: exp backoff + jitter, max 4 attempts. Left a TODO to add circuit-breaker example if time permits.
